newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Triple P to restructure company.
newsitem.headline: Triple P to restructure company.

text.p: Dutch software and services group Triple P said on Friday it was to restructure the company and said it would focus on profitable activities.
"The firm should concentrate on promising and profitable activities," it said in a statement.
The company said earlier it made a second quarter 1997 net loss of 24.8 million guilders versus a profit of 0.24 million in the same period of 1996.
Triple P said in a statement it would take several measures to become profitable again, concentrating on a few promising activities.
It will shed two business units and a few segments of its software solutions activities.
"Beside this, we have identified other activities that should be ended," it said, without giving further details.
It said the financial position had been strengthened by issuing 6,380,000 ordinary shares and 24,000,000 cumulative preference shares.
It said it also acquired a 50 percent stake in Gesellschaft fur Medizinische Datenverarbeitung (GMD), a German firm specialised in medical software applications, for 4.5 million guilders.
"From January 1, 1997 we will participate in the earnings per share profit of GMD," it said.

"We have put in place highly motivated management committed to restoring operating profitability and shareholders value," it said, adding management and employees will own approximately six percent of the outstanding shares of the company.
